questions.question: A boy with a history of a fall from a tree presents with a lurching gait and dragging of his feet. Which of the following structures are involved?

suspectLines.text: The structure involved in causing lurching gait in the child is gluteus medius, marked as 2.

questions.explanation:
The structure involved in causing lurching gait in the child is gluteus medius, marked as 2.

Gluteus medius originates from the outer surface of the ilium between the anterior and posterior gluteal lines and inserts on the lateral surface of the greater trochanter. It is supplied by the superior gluteal nerve.

Gluteus medius and minimus are powerful abductors of the hip joint. When the leg on one side is lifted, the gluteus medius and minimus on the opposite supported side exert traction on the hip bone and raise the pelvis slightly on the unsupported side, helping maintain the trunk upright.

These actions are affected by superior gluteal nerve injury, fracture of the neck of femur, or loss of normal shaft angulation. With paralysis, the pelvis sinks on the unsupported normal side when standing on the affected limb, producing a positive Trendelenburg sign and a characteristic lurch toward the affected side with contralateral pelvic drop.

Other options described by the source: 1 is gluteus maximus; 3 is piriformis; 4 is the sciatic nerve.

questions.question: The anterior compartment of the leg contains all of the following muscles except:

suspectLines.text: Peroneus brevis belongs to the lateral compartment of the leg.

questions.explanation:
Peroneus brevis belongs to the lateral compartment of the leg.

Anterior-compartment muscles produce dorsiflexion and include extensor digitorum longus, extensor hallucis longus, tibialis anterior and peroneus tertius.

Posterior-compartment muscles produce plantar flexion and are separated into superficial and deep groups. The superficial group contains gastrocnemius, plantaris and soleus. The deep group contains popliteus, flexor digitorum longus, flexor hallucis longus and tibialis posterior. The lateral compartment contains peroneus longus and peroneus brevis and produces eversion.

questions.question: Which of the following muscles is known as triceps surae?

suspectLines.text: The source notes that the main bulk of the calf is formed by gastrocnemius, plantaris and soleus, which constitute the superficial flexor group of the posterior compartment of the leg.

questions.explanation:
Gastrocnemius (two heads) and soleus are collectively known as triceps surae. They form a powerful muscular mass whose main function is plantar flexion of the foot.

The source notes that the main bulk of the calf is formed by gastrocnemius, plantaris and soleus, which constitute the superficial flexor group of the posterior compartment of the leg.

questions.question: Which of the following passive movements causes pain in a patient suffering from deep posterior compartment syndrome?

suspectLines.text: Dorsiflexion of the foot causes pain in deep posterior compartment syndrome of the leg.

questions.explanation:
Dorsiflexion of the foot causes pain in deep posterior compartment syndrome of the leg.

All tibial fractures should be monitored for compartment syndrome; severe pain is the most important clinical feature, and swelling, blistering and skin necrosis are late features.

The source summarizes: superficial and deep posterior compartment syndromes cause pain on passive dorsiflexion of the foot and toe extension; anterior compartment syndrome causes pain on passive plantar flexion of the foot and toe flexion; lateral compartment syndrome causes pain on passive foot inversion.
